**CFTC and ETF Report** _A weekly update of futures and exchange traded fund activity._ 

- Gold saw frantic ranges last week, touching $1765 basis December gold at one point before rallying back to former levels of congestion around $1825. Given the extra-ordinary attention paid to Greece, and the possible consequence not only for other ‘southern’ Eurozone member states of a Greek default, but for the very integrity of the European project, gold has been restrained, and that  implies that wise longs have been happy to let get go of their longs into a willing marketplace. Silver and the PGMs suffered partly through gold’s fall, and partly through a sequence of poor economic data. We see money being pulled out of the precious space and tend to assume it is a natural response to margin pressure, but it is worth nothing that money is flowing out of equities rapidly. 

- Overall, we are seeing declines in investor positioning under the pressure of volatility and price declines., as investor sentiment struggles against the headwinds of Europe, poor US growth, and some concerns over China—rising inflation and slowing growth there combined with regional debt burdens? 

• Gold and Silver saw ETF inflows as the macro picture still remains gold supportive in a time of negative real interest rates and heightened risk, with silver largely along for the ride. The PGMS are none the less underperforming in response to rational economic concerns—the same ones that may serve to underpin gold.

It was difficult to see what the driver was when so many of the factors governing gold’s recent rally remained in place, however, which so many reasons ‘to buy’ it also made sense for healthy longs to take profit whilst those factors remained in place—particularly as ‘headline risk’ of Eurozone leaders launching an all out assault to save Greece, and by extension the Euro, was high. The market essentially traded ‘risk off’ before looking over-sold and finishing the week with what looks like a corrective move back to $1825 Decembers. - Platinum dropped to levels not seen since early August last week as Euro zone disruption displaced concerns over supply, and cost pressures. $1770 seems to be the area where buying interest turns the selling around, although $1755-1760 seems even more secure as a support level in the short term. With a week when core retail sales, unemployment, the Empire State manufacturing index and the Philly Fed all came in looking gloomy indeed, and there was fresh movement to break the deadlock on US home foreclosure, and it was not surprising that Platinum was struggling. - Net long speculative interest in platinum on NYMEX ounces dropped by almost 90,000 Tozs. Is it again a question of trading around the Profit taking on the Platinum-gold spread, or symptomatic of wider risk reduction? - Platinum ETF holdings decreased very slightly over the week. ETF holdings are nonetheless very close to their all-time highs however. 4 **Mitsui Global Precious Metals | CFTC and ETF Weekly Report** **19 September 2011** ## **Palladium CFTC data to 13 September 2011; ETF data to 16 September 2011.** |**Exchange (Nymex and TOCOM) and ETF Palladium Investment (oz)**| |---| |**Date**|**Nymex**
